Early expensive cars already did this.

When cars replaced horses in the early 20th Century, there were craftspeople called "Coachbuilders" that used to build ornate stagecoaches (to be pulled by horses.)

In Europe, after cars appeared, when you bought a nice (expensive) car, you'd often have to choose which coachbuilder to use. (You only purchased chassis and engine from car company, then coachbuilder built the passenger cabin.

Most of these coachbuilders would create luggage in the same material as the interior.

IAMA former Flight Attendant for a certain somewhat infamous European "Low cost Carrier"

• How long were you a flight attendant?
  • What's the best place you visited, and why?
  • What's the worst place you visited, and why was it Paris?
  • Can you share any travel tips/hacks?

• Almost 3 years
  • Best place was probably Crete, although it wasn't on the job because we only stayed at the destination for 25-40 minutes and then went back
  • Worst place was definitely Paris. Although it's mainly because their airports and ground staff are lazy and slow.
  • Travel tips...I'd say travel light. If you're gonna be traveling on a low cost bring food or don't complain about the prices because we have no say on them nor on how much is on the plane, also understand that flight attendants are there for your safety the rest is just a side job we're stuck with :)

• How does one become a flight attendant? What sort of training is involved? Do you shadow with experienced ones or do they "Set you loose" once whatever education has concluded?
  • What are the best perks for you personally? I would think travel to exotic locales, but you have to work when traveling.
  • Are you male or female? Married, in a relationship, or single? If you have a significant other, do they travel with you sometimes (discount or free trips, etc)?
  • Worst passenger story? :) (or colleague story if there are any and you feel like sharing)

• For my airline you just go to an interview. Then you have about 4-6 weeks (can't remember exactly) of training, you go over emergency procedures, first-aid that sort of stuff. Once you finish that you have to do 12 flights with a crew and you just do some stuff to get used to it, it's pretty nerve-wrecking :)

  • We mostly traveled within Europe and stayed at the destination for only 25-40 minutes. But we did have pretty nice prices for tickets. I did enjoy it quite a bit.

  • I'm a guy, currently single. But last year when I had a gf we did go on a week vacation to Croatia and used my staff tickets. It was pretty great.

  • Worst passenger story was this drunk guy from Lithuania (I think) and the dude just got up about 500ft from the ground, wouldn't sit down because he didn't understand English. The guy landed standing up holding on to two seats, I was really surprised that he didn't just tip over during landing. Going from 180 mph to about 50 in 700ft seems pretty hard when you're sober let alone drunk.
If you could have done one thing differently in life, what would it be?
I was 24 when I started to learn English, I should have begun years before that.
